newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers majority stake in paper firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers majority stake in paper firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Chemical Industries and National Investment Bank on Sunday said they were privatising Simo/Middle East Paper company by offering investors between 10 and 75 percent of the firm.

The state companies said in a published announcement that the public offer of between 300,000 and 2,250,000 shares, of Simo's total three million shares, would open for two days from June 15 at a minimum price of 20 pounds ($6) per share.
The Holding Company for Chemical Industries currently owns 68.15 percent of Simo while the National Investment Bank has a 31.85 percent stake in the paper firm.
The state companies are also offering 300,000 shares or 10 percent of their stake in Simo/Middle East Paper to the firm's Employee Shareholder Association.
Individuals must apply for at least 100 shares while mutual funds and financial firms have a 1,000-share minimum.
Incentives for new shareholders include the dividend per share for the 1996/7 financial year, which Simo said would be 1.64 pounds, up from 1.14 pounds in 1995/6. The financial year ends on June 30.

Simo/Middle East Paper forecast net after-tax profit for 1996/7 to rise to 4.540 million pounds from 4.370 million in 1995/6. The firm expects 1997/8 net after-tax profit to total 5.460 million pounds.
Net sales are expected to fall to 38.177 million pounds from 39.823 million in 1995/6. Sales in 1997/8 are expected to rise to 41.850 million pounds.
Banque du Cairo and EFG/Hermes Brokerage are the agents for the sale.
The share offer is part of Egypt's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
